rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations and no d-states in the gap, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Strong ionicity and a deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the electronegativity-difference gap ladder.
Partially filled d bands add states near the Fermi level, narrowing gaps; this source relation had near-zero confidence, so it is downweighted and reversed.
Pnictides are weakly ionic covalent semiconductors; small electronegativity contrast yields small experimental gaps.

skill.hypothesis: Ranks anion chemistry by cation-anion electronegativity contrast and reverses the near-zero-confidence transition-metal source relation. Fails for d0 transition-metal oxides and defect-dominated measurements that deviate from the ionicity ordering.
